title: Jeremiah's Life Becomes a Warning
overview: The LORD tells Jeremiah to give up marriage, funerals and parties as a living sign of coming disaster, explains why it is coming, and still promises a future return home.

parts.label: No wife, no children (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: In a culture that prized marriage and big families, Jeremiah's staying single was a public signal that the coming disaster would make raising children a heartbreak. War, hunger and disease would leave so many dead that bodies would lie unburied, which was seen as the worst disgrace.

parts.label: No funerals, no feasts (vv. 5-9)
parts.note: Friends normally visited mourners with a funeral meal and a drink of wine to console them, and some cut themselves or shaved their heads in grief, even though Israel's law forbade it. Jeremiah must skip both mourning and celebrations, acting out a time when the LORD's love and pity are withdrawn and the sounds of weddings and laughter fall silent.

parts.label: The people ask why (vv. 10-13)
parts.note: The answer is that their ancestors left the LORD for other gods, and this generation has gone further, stubbornly refusing to listen. The punishment mirrors the wrong: people who chose other gods at home will be forced from the land and left serving other gods in exile.

parts.label: A greater return home (vv. 14-15)
parts.note: In the middle of the warnings comes a promise that one day the people will be brought back from the north, most likely meaning Babylon, whose armies came from that direction. That rescue would be remembered as even greater than the escape from Egypt, the founding story Israelites used when swearing an oath.

parts.label: Fishers and hunters (vv. 16-18)
parts.note: Invading armies are pictured as fishermen netting people and hunters chasing them into every cave, so no one escapes and nothing is hidden from God. Paying back double most likely means paying back in full, and the dead things that pollute the land are probably the lifeless idols themselves, though scholars read both phrases in more than one way.

parts.label: Nations drop their idols (vv. 19-21)
parts.note: Jeremiah prays to the LORD as his safe place and pictures people from every land admitting that their human-made gods were never gods at all. The LORD answers that this time he will show his power so clearly that people will know who he really is.

think: What would it take for you to believe a warning that almost everyone around you was ignoring?
